title: IELTS Academic (Listening & Reading)
issuer: British Council / IDP / Cambridge Assessment English

exam.scoring: Band 1-9 with 0.5 increments (Listening and Reading sections)

content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the IELTS Academic format, covering the multiple-choice portions of the Listening (40 questions) and Reading (40 questions) sections; Writing and Speaking components are not multiple-choice and are not represented here. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A passage about rooftop beekeeping notes that supporters praise the pollination of urban gardens while critics warn that dense hives can spread disease and outcompete wild bees. What is the writer's balanced conclusion about urban hives?
options: Urban hives can aid pollination but need careful management to limit disease and competition.
Urban hives are banned in most large cities.
Urban hives have no measurable effect on gardens or parks.
Urban hives always destroy wild bee populations.
items.explanation: The passage credits the hives with pollinating gardens and parks yet warns of disease and competition with wild bees, so the balanced view is benefit combined with careful management.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A news article reports that a city cycling plan will convert two central traffic lanes into protected bike routes and add 400 secure parking spaces by next spring. According to the text, how many secure parking spaces will be added?
items.explanation: The text states plainly that 400 secure parking spaces will be added by next spring, so the other figures are not supported by the passage.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: In a tutorial the student says the Great Barrier Reef was chosen for the project but admits, "I am worried I have taken on too much." The tutor replies, "Then narrow your focus to coral bleaching on one reef section." What does the tutor advise the student to do?
options: Reduce the scope of the project.
Abandon the project for this term.
items.explanation: The tutor tells the student to narrow the focus to one reef section, which means reducing the scope rather than changing the topic entirely.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A geography passage explains that the term carrying capacity describes the maximum population an environment can sustain without degradation. In the text, carrying capacity means what?
options: The number of species present in a habitat.
The speed at which a population grows.
The total area covered by an ecosystem.
The largest population an environment can support without being damaged.
items.explanation: The passage defines carrying capacity as the maximum population an environment can sustain without degradation, which matches the option about supporting a population without damage.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A research summary reports that participants who slept fewer than six hours performed 20 per cent worse on memory tasks than those who slept eight hours. How much worse did the short sleepers perform?
items.explanation: The summary states that short sleepers performed 20 per cent worse on memory tasks, which is the figure given directly in the passage.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: In a lecture the speaker states, "Contrary to popular belief, the Great Wall was not a single continuous structure, since it was built and rebuilt by several dynasties." Which misconception does the speaker correct?
options: That the wall can be seen from space
That the wall was one continuous structure built all at once
That the wall was made of stone only
That the wall is longer than any other
items.explanation: The speaker says the wall was built and rebuilt by several dynasties, correcting the belief that it was a single continuous structure built all at once.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A journal summary notes that although a medication reduced symptoms in trials, the authors caution that the sample was small and drawn from a single region. What can be inferred about the results?
options: They show the medication is useless.
They are promising but need confirmation in larger studies.
They are final and apply to everyone.
items.explanation: The authors warn that the sample was small and from one region, so the results are encouraging but require validation in larger, broader studies.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A research report states that the results were inconclusive because the team could not rule out chance. In the passage, the word inconclusive most nearly means what?
options: Not leading to a definite conclusion
items.explanation: The report explains that chance could not be ruled out, so inconclusive means the findings do not lead to a definite conclusion.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: At the library counter the student asks whether the book can be reserved once it returns, and the librarian answers, "Certainly, and we will email you." What does the librarian agree to do?
options: Reserve the book and send an email when it is available
Sell the book to the student
Order a new copy from another library
items.explanation: The librarian says certainly and promises an email, which means reserving the book and notifying the student when it returns.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A climate article reports that satellite records show the Antarctic ice sheet has been losing mass at an accelerating rate since the 1990s. What does the text say about the ice sheet since the 1990s?
options: It has gained mass in winter only
It has been losing mass at an accelerating rate
It has stayed exactly the same
items.explanation: The passage states directly that the ice sheet has been losing mass at an accelerating rate since the 1990s, so the other options contradict the text.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: An article about modern employment argues that many employers now value adaptable skills over fixed job titles because roles change faster than training programmes can be rewritten. What do these employers increasingly prefer?
options: Workers trained in a single task
items.explanation: The article says employers value adaptable skills over fixed job titles, so they increasingly prefer workers who can adapt as roles change.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: In a history lecture the speaker says the wheel was probably invented for pottery before it was used for transport. What does the speaker say about the wheel?
options: It was invented in the twentieth century
It was never used for pottery
It was first used for making pottery
items.explanation: The speaker states the wheel was probably invented for pottery before transport, so its first use was making pottery.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A passage observes that the evidence for the theory remains tenuous and rests on a handful of ambiguous artefacts. In the passage, tenuous is closest in meaning to what?
items.explanation: The evidence is said to rest on a few ambiguous artefacts, so tenuous means weak and not firmly established.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A museum notice states that the new wing opens in March and that entry is free for students on weekdays. When is entry free for students?
items.explanation: The notice says entry is free for students on weekdays, so weekends, March-only and holidays are not supported by the text.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A student tells an adviser the assignment is late because a laptop failed and the file was lost, and the adviser replies, "Submit a mitigating-circumstances form and we will consider an extension." What does the adviser recommend?
items.explanation: The adviser asks for a mitigating-circumstances form before considering an extension, so that is the recommended step.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A feature on community gardens argues that they do more than grow food, since they also build neighbourhood ties and give residents a shared purpose. What main value does the feature emphasise?
options: Social benefits as well as food
items.explanation: The feature stresses neighbourhood ties and shared purpose, so it emphasises social benefits in addition to growing food.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A report states that of the 300 participants in a mindfulness course, 45 per cent reported improved concentration. What percentage reported improved concentration?
items.explanation: The report gives the figure as 45 per cent of participants, which is stated directly rather than inferred.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: In a marine biology lecture the speaker says coral reefs occupy less than one per cent of the ocean floor yet support about a quarter of all marine species. What does the speaker say about coral reefs?
options: They cover most of the ocean floor
They cover under one per cent of the ocean floor but support about a quarter of marine species
They are found only in cold water
items.explanation: The speaker states the reefs cover less than one per cent of the ocean floor yet support about a quarter of marine species, exactly matching this option.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A business report notes that the company announced record sales yet its share price fell, suggesting investors doubted the figures could be sustained. What does this suggest?
options: Sales were lower than last year
Investors doubted the sales could continue
items.explanation: The report links the falling share price to doubts that the record sales could be sustained, so investors doubted the sales could continue.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A policy analysis says the rules were implemented piecemeal, with different measures taking effect in different regions at different times. In the passage, piecemeal means what?
options: According to a single detailed plan
Gradually in separate stages rather than all at once
items.explanation: The passage describes measures taking effect in different regions at different times, so piecemeal means gradually in separate stages.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: An employee asks to attend a training conference in June, and the manager replies that it clashes with the audit and asks whether the employee could attend the September session instead. What is the manager's response?
options: Attend the June session as planned
items.explanation: The manager notes the June clash and suggests the September session, so the response is to attend in September instead.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A local history text explains that the bridge, completed in 1890, was the longest suspension span in the world for two decades. For how long was it the world's longest suspension span?
items.explanation: The text says the bridge held the record for two decades, which is twenty years, not two years or twenty months.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A music article argues that streaming has changed not only how music is sold but also how songs are written, with artists front-loading catchy hooks to hold listeners in the first few seconds. What does the article claim streaming has changed?
options: Both the market and the way songs are composed
items.explanation: The article says streaming changed both how music is sold and how songs are written, so both the market and composition are affected.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: In an ecology lecture the speaker explains that bees share the direction and distance of food through a movement known as the waggle dance. How does the speaker say bees share information about food?
options: By making a loud buzzing sound
By leaving a scent trail only
Through a movement called the waggle dance
items.explanation: The speaker names the waggle dance as the way bees communicate the direction and distance of food.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A history passage contrasts a sudden collapse with the slower decline of the civilisation, whose cities thinned out over several generations. What does the writer contrast with a sudden collapse?
options: A gradual decline over several generations
items.explanation: The passage contrasts a sudden collapse with a decline spread over several generations, which is a gradual decline.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A transport survey found that commuters who cycled took an average of 32 minutes, while those who drove took 41 minutes. On average, how much longer was the drive than the cycle?
items.explanation: Subtracting the 32-minute cycle time from the 41-minute drive time gives a difference of nine minutes.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A customer reports that the software keeps crashing when large files are opened, and support replies, "Please update to version 4.2 and send us the crash log." What does support ask the customer to do?
options: Update the software and send a crash log
items.explanation: Support requests an update to version 4.2 and the crash log, so the customer is asked to update and send the log.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A media essay contends that online reviews reward confidence over accuracy, so readers should cross-check several sources before deciding. What does the essay advise readers to do?
options: Read only one review per product
items.explanation: The essay warns that reviews reward confidence over accuracy and advises checking several sources, which matches cross-checking.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A text outlines a four-stage water-treatment process in which screening removes large debris, sedimentation lets particles settle, filtration passes water through sand, and chlorination disinfects it. Which stage removes large debris?
items.explanation: The process description assigns the removal of large debris to the first stage, screening, while the other stages handle particles and disinfection.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A table compares rainfall in two towns. Town A records 800 mm in a normal year and Town B records 500 mm, while in a drought year both figures fall by 40 per cent. In a drought year, how much rain does Town A receive?
items.explanation: A 40 per cent fall from 800 mm leaves 60 per cent, which is 480 mm, so Town A receives 480 mm in the drought year.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A profile describes three applicants. Maya has ten years of finance experience but no management training, Dev has managed teams but is new to finance, and Priya has both finance experience and management training. Which applicant best fits a role requiring both?
items.explanation: Only Priya has both finance experience and management training, so she alone satisfies the two stated requirements of the role.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: In a campus audio guide the speaker explains that the fire exit is at the end of the corridor, past the lifts, and is marked with a green sign. Where is the fire exit located?
options: At the end of the corridor beyond the lifts
items.explanation: The guide places the fire exit at the end of the corridor past the lifts, so the location beyond the lifts is correct.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A line graph traces a company's profits, which rise each year from 2019 to 2021 and then fall sharply in 2022. What trend does the graph show?
options: Steady growth followed by a sharp decline
items.explanation: Profits rise through 2021 and then drop sharply in 2022, giving steady growth followed by a sharp decline.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A leaflet explains how to appeal a parking fine. You must first pay the fine, then submit an online appeal within 28 days, and finally await the review decision. What must be done before submitting the appeal?
items.explanation: The leaflet orders the steps so that paying the fine comes before submitting the appeal, which is then followed by the decision.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A library guide describes three zones. The silent zone bans all talking, the group zone permits discussion, and the computer zone allows quiet typing only. In which zone is quiet typing permitted?
items.explanation: The guide permits quiet typing only in the computer zone, while the silent and group zones are described by talking rules.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A price table lists three ticket types. Standard costs 20, Student costs 12, and Family costs 45 for four people. Which ticket offers the lowest cost per person?
options: They cost the same per person
items.explanation: The family ticket costs 45 for four people, which is about 11.25 each, lower than the standard 20 and the student 12 per person.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A pie chart divides household spending, with housing taking 40 per cent, food 20 per cent, transport 15 per cent, and other costs 25 per cent. Which category accounts for the largest share?
items.explanation: Housing takes 40 per cent, which is larger than food at 20, transport at 15 and other costs at 25, so housing is the largest share.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A method section states that in the experiment the mixture is heated to 80 degrees, stirred for ten minutes, then cooled to room temperature before testing. What is done immediately after heating the mixture to 80 degrees?
options: It is stirred for ten minutes
It is cooled to room temperature
items.explanation: The sequence places stirring for ten minutes directly after heating, with cooling and testing occurring later in the method.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: In a venue audio guide the speaker says the registration desk is on the ground floor beside the main entrance, opposite the cafe. What is directly opposite the registration desk?
items.explanation: The guide says the desk is beside the main entrance and opposite the cafe, so the cafe is directly opposite.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A prospectus describes three courses. Course X is for beginners, Course Y for intermediate students, and Course Z for advanced students who already hold a certificate. Which course is designed for learners who already hold a certificate?
items.explanation: The prospectus reserves Course Z for advanced students who already hold a certificate, while X and Y target beginners and intermediate learners.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A bar chart compares four energy sources, where solar provides 10 units, wind 15 units, coal 50 units, and gas 25 units. Which source provides exactly half as much as coal?
items.explanation: Coal provides 50 units, so half of that is 25 units, which is the amount shown for gas.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A process description covers paper recycling. The paper is sorted, shredded, pulped, and then pressed into new sheets. Which step comes immediately before pressing?
items.explanation: The process lists sorting, shredding and pulping before pressing, so pulping is the step immediately before pressing.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A volunteering form matches people to tasks by interest. Those who enjoy the outdoors join the gardening team, those skilled with computers join the data team, and those who like cooking join the kitchen team. Which team suits a volunteer who is skilled with computers?
items.explanation: The form directs people skilled with computers to the data team, so that is the matching team for such a volunteer.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A table reports course completion, showing that of 200 enrolled students 150 completed and 50 withdrew. What proportion of the enrolled students withdrew?
items.explanation: Fifty of 200 students withdrew, and 50 divided by 200 equals one quarter of the enrolled group.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A campus audio guide gives directions to the lecture theatre. After entering the main building, you turn left at the stairs, and the theatre is the second door on the right. After turning left at the stairs, where is the theatre?
options: The second door on the right
At the top of the stairs
The first door on the left
items.explanation: The guide specifies the second door on the right after turning left at the stairs, so that is the theatre's position.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A guide describes a job application sequence. There is first an online form, then an interview, then a written test, and finally an offer decision. Which stage follows the interview?
items.explanation: The sequence places the written test immediately after the interview, with the offer decision coming last of all.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A gallery map lists four exhibits. Exhibit 1 is a painting, Exhibit 2 a sculpture, Exhibit 3 a photograph, and Exhibit 4 a video installation. Which exhibit is a video installation?
items.explanation: The map identifies the video installation as Exhibit 4, while the others are a painting, a sculpture and a photograph.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A line graph charts the temperature over a day. It peaks at 3pm at 24 degrees and reaches its lowest at 5am at 8 degrees. What is the difference between the day's highest and lowest temperatures?
items.explanation: The highest temperature is 24 degrees and the lowest is 8 degrees, so the difference is 16 degrees.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: An assembly manual explains how to build a shelf. The brackets are fixed to the wall, the boards are attached to the brackets, and then all the screws are tightened. What is done immediately after fixing the brackets to the wall?
options: Attach the boards to the brackets
items.explanation: The manual attaches the boards to the brackets straight after fixing the brackets, and only then tightens the screws.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A notice describes parking arrangements. The staff car park is behind the building and is reached through the side gate on Mill Street. How is the staff car park reached?
options: Through the side gate on Mill Street
items.explanation: The notice says the car park behind the building is reached through the side gate on Mill Street, so that is the route.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A timetable lists three trains. The 8.05 train arrives at 9.20, the 8.40 arrives at 9.50, and the 9.10 arrives at 10.30. Which train makes the quickest journey?
items.explanation: The journey times are 75 minutes for the 8.05, 70 minutes for the 8.40 and 80 minutes for the 9.10, so the 8.40 is quickest.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A stacked bar chart shows a budget. Salaries take 60 per cent, equipment 20 per cent, travel 10 per cent, and training 10 per cent. Which two categories together equal the equipment share?
items.explanation: Equipment is 20 per cent, and travel plus training is 10 plus 10, which also equals 20 per cent, so those two match the equipment share.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A comparison of three suppliers weighs cost against speed. Supplier A is cheapest but slowest, Supplier B is fastest but dearest, and Supplier C is moderate in both. Which supplier is best for a buyer who prioritises speed?
items.explanation: A buyer who prioritises speed should choose the fastest supplier, which the comparison identifies as Supplier B, despite its higher price.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A procedure explains soil testing. The samples are collected, then dried, then the bags are labelled, and finally the samples are sent to the laboratory. Which action comes immediately after drying the samples?
items.explanation: The procedure places labelling the bags directly after drying, with sending to the laboratory as the final step.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A safety announcement states that the emergency assembly point is the open field west of the main gate, away from all buildings. Where is the emergency assembly point?
options: In the open field west of the main gate
items.explanation: The announcement locates the assembly point in the open field west of the main gate, away from the buildings.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A survey records how 400 people travel. Of these, 160 drive, 120 take the bus, 80 cycle, and 40 walk. Which two modes together account for exactly half of the respondents?
items.explanation: Half of 400 is 200, and taking the bus at 120 plus cycling at 80 equals 200, so those two modes make up exactly half.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: Two colleagues discuss a deadline. One says the deadline is Friday, and the other replies, "I am well aware of the deadline." What does the second speaker's reply suggest?
items.explanation: The phrase well aware signals that the reminder was unnecessary, which conveys mild irritation rather than thanks or confusion.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: In a lecture the speaker says, "Some claim this method is flawless, but I would treat that claim with caution." How does the speaker feel about the claim that the method is flawless?
items.explanation: Advising caution about the claim shows the speaker doubts it, which means the speaker is sceptical rather than convinced.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A manager comments that if the figures do not improve by June the project will have to be reconsidered. Which option best paraphrases the manager's meaning?
options: The figures are certain to improve
June is the project's start date
The project's future depends on better figures by June
The project has already been cancelled
items.explanation: The manager makes the project's future conditional on improved figures by June, so its continuation depends on those figures.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A caller begins a phone call by saying, "Sorry to bother you, but could I possibly ask a quick question?" What is the caller's intention?
options: To ask politely for a moment of the listener's time
items.explanation: The apologetic, tentative phrasing is a polite request for a moment of the listener's attention, not a complaint or order.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A student says the film was too long, and the tutor replies, "I could not agree more, since the editing was poor." What is the tutor's opinion?
options: The tutor agrees the film was too long and poorly edited
The tutor thought the film was too short
The tutor has not seen the film
The tutor disagrees with the student
items.explanation: The reply could not agree more signals full agreement, and the tutor adds that the editing was poor, confirming the same view.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A resident says the new bus route is a real improvement, although the timetables are still confusing. What is the resident's overall attitude?
options: Broadly positive but critical of the timetables
items.explanation: Calling the route a real improvement is positive, while the complaint about timetables tempers it, giving a broadly positive but critical attitude.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A doctor tells a patient that the tests are clear but that a follow-up appointment in three months would still be wise. Why does the doctor want a follow-up appointment?
options: To repeat the same tests immediately
To check the patient's progress as a precaution
items.explanation: With clear tests but a wise follow-up, the doctor wants a precautionary check on progress rather than to repeat tests or cancel results.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: An article evaluates a policy and says it has not delivered on its promises. Which option best paraphrases the author's meaning?
options: The policy has no stated aims
The policy has worked better than expected
The policy has failed to achieve what it promised
items.explanation: Saying a policy has not delivered on its promises means it failed to achieve what it promised, not that it exceeded expectations.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A critic reviews a novel and says it is ambitious, but that its characters never feel fully real. What is the critic's main reservation?
items.explanation: Saying the characters never feel fully real is a criticism that they are underdeveloped, which is the critic's main reservation.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A volunteer approaches a passer-by and asks whether they would mind filling in a short survey that takes two minutes. What is the volunteer's purpose?
options: To persuade the person to complete a brief survey
items.explanation: The volunteer asks the passer-by to fill in a short survey, so the purpose is to persuade them to complete that brief survey.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A headteacher reports that attendance has risen and says, "I am delighted, even if the figures are modest." How does the headteacher feel?
options: Pleased despite the modest size of the improvement
items.explanation: The word delighted shows pleasure, and the concession about modest figures means the headteacher is pleased despite the small scale.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A report concludes that the scheme is worth pursuing provided costs are controlled. Which option best paraphrases the report's conclusion?
options: The scheme should be expanded without limits
The scheme has no cost implications
The scheme should be abandoned at once
The scheme should continue if spending is kept in check
items.explanation: Worth pursuing provided costs are controlled means the scheme should continue only if spending is kept in check, not abandoned or unlimited.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A guest comments, "If I had known there was no parking, I would have taken the train." What is the guest implying?
options: The lack of parking made the journey awkward
items.explanation: The conditional shows the guest would have chosen the train had they known about the missing parking, so the lack of parking made the journey awkward.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: An editor tells a writer that the argument is appealing but the evidence needs strengthening before publication. What is the editor's view?
options: The piece should be published unchanged
The argument is good but the evidence is not yet strong enough
The argument is weak and should be dropped
items.explanation: The editor finds the argument appealing yet wants stronger evidence, so the argument is good but the evidence is not yet sufficient.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A resident says the festival was busier than ever and adds, "Honestly, that is a mixed blessing." What does the resident mean?
options: The crowds brought both benefits and problems
The festival was a complete failure
items.explanation: A mixed blessing contains both good and bad elements, so the larger crowds brought benefits as well as problems.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A candidate replies to a job offer by saying, "I appreciate the offer, but I would like a day to think it over." What is the candidate's intention?
options: To negotiate a higher salary at once
To delay a decision while considering the offer
items.explanation: Asking for a day to think it over shows the candidate wants to delay the decision while considering the offer, not accept or reject it now.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A lecturer remarks that the evidence is suggestive rather than conclusive. Which option best paraphrases the remark?
options: The evidence hints at a conclusion but does not prove it
The evidence is irrelevant to the topic
items.explanation: Suggestive rather than conclusive means the evidence points towards a conclusion without proving it, so it hints but does not prove.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A reviewer says that, for the price, the headphones are impressive, although the battery lags behind rivals. What is the reviewer's overall opinion?
options: Good value overall, with one weakness
items.explanation: Impressive for the price signals good value, while the battery weakness is a single drawback, giving a positive overall view with one flaw.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: An event organiser asks visitors to keep to the path because the meadow beyond is a protected habitat. Why does the organiser ask them to keep to the path?
options: To avoid damaging the path itself
To protect a sensitive natural area
items.explanation: The stated reason is that the meadow is a protected habitat, so keeping to the path protects a sensitive natural area.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A scientist comments on early results by saying, "I am hopeful, but let us be clear, the results are preliminary." What is the scientist's attitude?
items.explanation: Being hopeful while calling the results preliminary combines optimism with caution, so the attitude is cautiously optimistic.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A commentator says the new rules tilt the balance in favour of smaller firms. Which option best paraphrases the meaning?
options: The rules give smaller firms an advantage
The rules affect only large firms
items.explanation: Tilting the balance in favour of smaller firms means giving them an advantage, not harming or ignoring them.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Reading

items.stem: A neighbour asks whether the music could be turned down after eleven, explaining that there is an early start the next day. What is the neighbour's reason?
options: To complain about the volume only
To sleep before an early start the next day
items.explanation: The neighbour gives an early start the next day as the reason, so the request is aimed at sleeping before that early start.
items.reference: IELTS Academic Official Practice Materials - Listening

items.stem: A museum trustee tells a meeting that the museum must modernise or younger visitors simply will not come. What is the trustee arguing?
options: The museum needs to modernise to attract younger visitors
Younger visitors already attend in large numbers

items.stem: An author says that writing the sequel was harder than the first book but adds, "I am proud of it." What does the author convey?
options: The sequel was easy and disappointing
The author regrets writing at all
The sequel was difficult to write yet personally satisfying
items.explanation: The author describes the sequel as harder yet is proud of it, conveying that it was difficult but personally satisfying.
